Newton's Method

CurvesLimitsAlgebra
Game: Pick a starting place on the curve and watch straight lines walk you down to where the curve crosses the line in the middle.
How to play: Click anywhere on the picture to choose where to start (click again to clear). Change how many steps to draw. Tick "Show points" to see little squares you can drag to bend the curve.

Square roots: the page's example


  


  

    Look for the math
    

      
Newton's method turns "solve f(x) = 0" into a string of easy problems: where does a straight line meet the axis? The surprise is how fast it works when it works, and how badly it can fail.


      
The tangent trick

      
At xn the tangent to the graph is y = f(xn) + (x - xn) f'(xn). It meets the axis at xn+1 = xn - f(xn) / f'(xn). On this page the curve is a cubic spline through eleven points, and its slope at each point is the spline's own derivative.


      
Square roots

      
With f(x) = x² - N the step becomes xn+1 = (xn + N/xn)/2, the average of a guess and N divided by the guess: Heron's method. The table above reproduces the page's figures to the last digit (1, 1.5, 1.4166666666666665, 1.4142156862745097, ...), and the fractions 3/2, 17/12, 577/408 are exact. After the first step every guess is at least √N, by the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality.


      
How fast, and when it fails

      
For x² - N the error obeys exactly a - xn+1 = -(a - xn)² / (2xn), so each step roughly squares the error: about twice as many correct digits each time. In general the factor is M = -f''(a) / (2f'(a)), and the page says the start must satisfy |a - x0| < 1/|M|. The test shows that this is a good rule of thumb near the root but not a guarantee: for x² - 2 the bound is 2.83, yet a start at -1.3, which is inside it, goes to the other root, -√2. Near a flat part of the curve the tangent is nearly level and the next point is thrown far away (try starting near the top of the hump), and for x³ - 2x + 2 a start at 0 bounces between 0 and 1 forever.


      
Start at x = 4.5 with 4 steps and watch the points pile up at the crossing. Then start near x = 0.6, the top of the hump.
